## 2026-08-10 · VOIX-VITRINE — playback that asked a player with nothing loaded to start · IN-REVIEW (branch, awaiting founder)
**Founder report:** « On ma vitrine in shop+ when I record an audio and want to play it back it's not working. »

**THIS IS THE SECOND HALF OF A BUG WHOSE FIRST HALF WAS ALREADY FIXED.** `voice-capture.ts` already carries the silent-switch fix — `setAudioModeAsync` sets the WHOLE mode rather than merging, so an earlier call had been dropping `playsInSilentMode` back to false and iOS played the take at zero volume. That was real and it shipped. It did not finish the job.

**FOUND:** `play()` called `p.replace({ uri: url })` and then `p.play()` on the very next line. `replace()` hands the player a new source; **loading it is asynchronous.** `play()` on a player with nothing loaded returns without error and without sound. Whether anything was heard depended on a race the code never acknowledged — a short local take on a fast phone sometimes won it, which is exactly why this read as intermittent rather than broken.

**FIXED:** playback now waits for the player's own word. `isLoaded` is the fact (`expo-audio` `AudioModule.types.d.ts` l.44 — « whether the player is finished loading »), and it arrives on the same `playbackStatusUpdate` the listener already reads. Both roads are covered and neither can double up: a `lance` flag starts playback exactly once, whether the player was ALREADY loaded (she listens to the same take twice — no further status may arrive, so waiting for one would hang) or becomes loaded a moment later.

**⚠ EVIDENCE, STATED HONESTLY — AND THIS IS THE NEW LAW'S FIRST EXCEPTION.** `voice-capture.ts` is the NATIVE adapter: it imports `expo-audio` at module scope and is by construction never imported by a test (the file's own header states this, and the Metro-safe law requires it). The pure reducer and the demo double in `./voice.ts` are what the Node tests exercise, and they do not model loading at all. So this fix is gated by **tsc only**, exactly as the file was designed to be, and is **founder-device-verified** per the standing RN device-matrix note.
- **What that means for the 2026-08-10 screen-walk law:** it is not evaded here, it does not reach. The law binds SCREENS; this is a native module adapter behind a seam, with no screen in it. **The screen that drives it — the voice sheet — still has no walk, because this repo has no harness.** That obligation stands and is recorded in the STANDING ORDER entry below.

**Pending:** merge + deploy approval. Reseller-app changes reach the founder through its own preview publish.

## 2026-08-10 · STANDING ORDER — the screen is DRIVEN, never only read · LAW
**Founder:** « Make it a law from now on every build and fix should uses this tool for tests before merge and deploy ask. »

Written into `§6bis` of `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in **all four repos**, byte-identical (`b0c23c14`) — the parity rule of §6.

**What it says, in short:** any build or fix touching a user-facing screen ends with a RENDU-RÉEL walk — mount the real screen, press the real controls, assert the person reaches the next step — before merge and deploy are asked for. Every new screen gets a walk in the same slice that builds it, and **every screen bug the founder reports gets its walk written FIRST, red, before the fix.** Its bound is absolute: it may never claim anything about appearance.

**⚠ WHAT THIS REPO OWES.** The reference implementation is the Séra rider app (`apps/rider-app/test/rendu.tsx` + `rendu-course.test.tsx` + `rendu-harness.test.ts` + `test/doubles/`). **No harness exists in this repo yet.** The order is explicit: the first slice that touches a screen here BUILDS the equivalent, or says plainly in the report that it did not and why. Silently falling back to source scans is the thing the order forbids.

**The slice sequence is now:** tests + typecheck + gate board green → **the screen walk** → the end-to-end seam test against the real service → the ONE fresh-context verifier pass → commit + push → report, then WAIT.

## 2026-08-06 · CI FLAKE, recorded not papered over — `cliente.spec.ts:440` C5 sentence-orphan sweep
- **Same commit `87799ba`, two runs, opposite results.** Run 31064422388 FAILED (1 of 88 Playwright tests); run 31064768627 on the **identical sha** SUCCEEDED. Nothing changed between them.
- **The commit cannot have caused it:** `git show 87799ba --name-only` is 8 files, all under `scripts/` and `gates/`. No app source, no CSS, no component. A gate script cannot change how text wraps in a browser. The three preceding heads (`055b7fb`, `632294d`, `3d20d9c`) all passed CI.
- **The assertion:** `cliente.spec.ts:649` — « basket 19 753 086: the CTA was not swept — it is a text block by display, or it stopped wrapping ».
- **Why this test specifically:** it is the font-UNPINNED variant. Its two siblings at `:825` — « face PINNED (face réelle) » and « (repli) » — both PASSED in the same run. The app ships `font-display: optional`, so the real face either arrives before first paint or does not, and the text metrics differ between the two. Whether the CTA wraps at that basket width depends on which face won the race.
- **This family has bitten before:** a prior slice is titled « C5 orphan under fallback metrics — fix the sentence, make the sweep face-deterministic ». The pinned variants were the fix; `:440` was left unpinned and is the residue.
- **NOT FIXED, deliberately, and flagged to the founder.** Editing a test so CI goes green is the failure mode of « make CI green » over « make it true ». Recommendation: pin the face in `:440` exactly as `:825` already does, as its own small slice — a flaky test on a MONEY screen is worse than a missing one, because it teaches everyone to re-run instead of read.

### SP6.3 (rounds 2–3) — the founder ruled both questions, and both are built

- **FOUNDER RULING 2026-08-04:** « on question 1 and 2 go ahead with your recommendation, and once everything is green merge and deploy all ». Both §7 triggers closed by him, including the `contracts/` change.

**Q1 — the buyer rung is enforced at ORDER CREATE.**
- §6.1 says « evaluated at quote »; four of its five conditions genuinely are. The fifth is about the BUYER and at quote this service knows of none — her phone arrives one step later with the dispatch contact (BC-1a, `order-do.ts` `CONTACT_KEY`). So the rung is read where its key exists, **still before any money moves and before any custody** (Law #3 untouched).
- **`BuyerLadderDO`, one instance per buyer, named `ladder:{cleAcheteur(phone)}`.** The DO name IS the per-buyer lock: two refusals for the same woman serialise with no transaction anywhere, and a refusal for a different woman cannot reach her record. It holds only the canonical `PayAtDoorEligibility` — no money, no order, no contact — and it DECIDES nothing: `appliquerRefus` decides, the object stores.
- **`cleAcheteur` carries the whole ruling.** « 70 12 34 56 », « +226 70123456 », « 00226-70-12-34-56 » are one woman and key identically; two different numbers never collide (pinned as its own control); a foreign number keeps its own digits rather than being refused; fewer than eight digits is unkeyable and the caller fails CLOSED.
- **`decideBuyerRung` EXTRACTED so there is ONE implementation.** Two gates disagreeing about « allowed » is how a buyer is offered the door at one step and refused at the next with no stated reason. Pinned: the extracted function and the full §6.1 gate agree on every ladder state.
- **A door order with NO contact gets its OWN refusal**, `contact_required_for_door`, deliberately not folded into the eligibility one — « we need your phone » is a field she can fill, « pay-at-door is unavailable » is not. A door delivery with no phone was never deliverable anyway.
- **FULL PREPAY IS NEVER TOUCHED.** Her history narrows one payment mode; it must never cost her the ability to buy. Asserted with a suspended buyer completing a prepay order.

**Q2 — canon v3.6.0 carries §6.5.**
- `RelatedPartySignalsSchema` splits the signals into **two disjoint enums** rather than one list with a severity field: `identity` (verified_identity · phone · wallet · own_account) auto-voids; `circumstantial` (device · household · landmark · shared_phone · network) reviews. **One list plus a severity would let a caller mark a household match as identity-grade; two enums make that unrepresentable, so the tier is structural.**
- **This is a statement about Burkina Faso, and the tests say so.** A shared handset, one courtyard, one landmark, one neighbourhood wifi — §6.5 calls these « often legitimate » in bold. All five stacked together is STILL a review; there is no threshold, and inventing one would auto-void a great many real households.

### SP6.3 — the §6.4 refusal ladder, its book, and §6.5's tier (BOTH QUESTIONS RULED)

- **THE ⚠ ON SP6.3 MEANS « get-the-architecture-right-here » (plan line 14), not a build gate** — so the slice is buildable, and the architecture question it warns about is exactly the one I hit.
- **BUILT: `packages/commerce-core/src/refusal-ladder.ts`** — §6.4 as a pure, replayable function `(record, reason, nowIso) -> record`, writing the CANONICAL `PayAtDoorEligibility`. It is correct under every option the founder may choose for the keying question below, which is why it was built first and alone.
- **THE LINE I CARED MOST ABOUT: `conformity_mismatch` NEVER COUNTS.** §6.2 lists « wrong / mismatch / damage / short » as a **valid rejection**. Counting it would punish a buyer for the platform's own failure and turn Option B's inspection right into a trap. Pinned, and the pin asserts through the REAL gate that the door is still open to her afterwards — not by reading fields.
- **`honest_absence` does not escalate** (§6.4 in bold) but IS recorded, so an operator can tell « a doorstep happened » from « no delivery was attempted ». **Terminal states do not re-escalate** — idempotence, so a replayed event cannot inflate a history.
- **⏳ TWO RUNGS THE SPEC DOES NOT MAKE IMPLEMENTABLE, safest-default + flagged, never invented:**
  - **Rung 1** — « higher delivery commitment **or** small product deposit »: an `or` between two mechanisms, neither built, and « small » names no franc. **Records the fault and changes nothing else.** Setting any deposit would refuse Option B outright (`decidePayAtDoorEligibility` refuses `requiredDeposit > 0`), i.e. rung-2 severity at rung 1. A first ordinary fault must not silently become a suspension.
  - **Rung 2** — « FULL_PREPAY for next 3 orders »: the spec counts ORDERS, canon's field is a TIMESTAMP, and adding an order-count field is a `contracts/` change (§7). Expressed in time; `PREPAY_ONLY_WINDOW_DAYS = 30` is **my flagged default, not a figure the spec gave**, and it is pinned so a silent change reddens.
- **MUTATION-TESTED, 6/6 reddened** — and one of them **survived the first attempt as a NO-OP** (a `requiredDeposit` insert that a later key overrode). Caught and re-run against the real branch: 2 red. **A mutation that does not change behaviour proves nothing, and reporting it as killed would have been a false claim about my own coverage.**
- **EVIDENCE:** commerce-core **111/111** (97 + 14) · storefront-service **464/464** · `scripts/run-gates.sh` **exit 0, zero `GATE FAILED`**.

- **BLOCKED-ON-FOUNDER — TWO §7 TRIGGERS, both verified in code rather than remembered:**
  1. **THE KEYING QUESTION (spec conflict, money/risk).** §6.1: « Option-B gate (**evaluated at quote**) … `PayAtDoorEligibility.state = allowed` ». But at quote Shop+ knows **no buyer**: `QuoteRequest` is slug · pid · paymentMode · zoneTo · attributionResellerId · requestKey, and the phone arrives one step later at ORDER CREATE (BC-1a, `order-do.ts` `CONTACT_KEY`). A ladder keyed to a buyer has no key at the moment the spec says to read it. **My recommendation: enforce the buyer rung at ORDER CREATE** — the first point where the key exists, still before any money moves and before custody, adding no self-declared input. The cost is honest and worth stating: she chooses Option B and is redirected at the last step. **I did NOT want to send her phone at quote time** — I removed the last self-declared §6.1 input this same session, and adding one back one slice later would undo it.
  2. **RELATED-PARTY (§6.5) HAS NO CANON SHAPE.** Verified: canon carries `attribution · commerce · common · custody · moderation · quote · settlement` and nothing for related-party. ### SP6.1 — earnings read model (net)

- **THE SCREEN WAS A DEMO, and worse than « Mes ventes » had been.** `screen === 'gains'` rendered `enAttenteNet()`, `payeSemaine()`, `gainsCards()` — all from `sales/ventes.ts` over `DEMO_SALES`. It showed **« Payé cette semaine »** on a platform that has never paid anyone.
- **TWO OF EIGHT RUNGS ARE DERIVABLE.** Projected (`payment_pending`) and Locked (`confirmed`, canon's first obligation state). Eligible waits on Séra's `delivery.validated.v1` — not flowing. Payable/Processing/Paid need a payout process; Held a hold; Adjusted an adjustment. **None exists in any repo.**
- **THE SIX RENDER, QUIET AND LABELLED « pas encore ».** Hiding them makes the ladder look complete at Locked and teaches her a confirmed sale is a paid one.
- **`atteignable` IS DERIVED, NOT DECLARED** — computed by exhausting `FeedState` through the mapping. A hand-written « these two are real » constant is the kind that goes stale silently; this one lights a rung up the day the mapping changes.
- **FULFILMENT DOES NOT MOVE MONEY.** `acceptedAt`/`readyAt` are deliberately unread: B+I-06 makes readiness the precondition for a pickup being REQUESTED, not a delivery. Pinned with a test asserting the rungs are byte-identical with and without them.
- **SP-I04 IS STRUCTURAL, not disciplined.** The only money entering is `resellerNet`, copied off the frozen Quote; no base, commission, markup or rate is on the shape, so `0.80×(C+M)` is unrepresentable. « 20 % real from launch » is therefore satisfied upstream — the fee was taken when the quote was signed and this surface can only show what survived it.
- **NOT AN ACCOUNT (Ten Laws #2).** No total, no « solde », no action. ONE hero — the Locked rung — because that is the single figure that is settled and unambiguously hers; a running total is what an account has. « Shop+ ne garde pas votre argent » renders on every ladder, asserted last in the notice list.
- **ONE FETCH, TWO SURFACES.** « Mes ventes » and « Mes gains » read the same rows, so they cannot disagree. The gains view is built from the RAW rows — `FeedVue` has already dropped everything non-confirmed, and the ladder's first rung is precisely those.

## 2026-08-02 · C5-ORPHELINS — the « flake » that was three real defects · IN REVIEW (branch `claude/buyer-pwa-standing-laws-nerljz`)
- **IT WAS NEVER A FLAKE.** CI run 30760780865 failed on « Vous inspectez le colis avant de payer le reste. » at **0.137** (bar 0.35); run 30760827619, on a tree differing by eighteen lines of JOURNAL.md, passed. Read as flake for three runs. **Cause, measured not guessed:** every face in `apps/buyer-pwa/src/fonts.css` is `font-display: optional`, which gives the webfont a ~100 ms window at load and, on a miss, keeps the fallback FOR THE WHOLE PAGE LIFE. The sweep measured whichever face won a race it did not control — and **both outcomes ship to real buyers**.
- **REPRODUCED TO THE DIGIT, locally:** pinning the same woff2 files as `font-display: block` gives **0.137**, the exact CI number; blocking the woff2 gives 0.426, which is what every green run had been measuring. The sentence needed **301px of a 299px box**, so « reste. » — the word naming what she still owes — stood alone on line two.
- **WAITING CANNOT FIX IT, and waiting was already tried.** `policesChargees` awaits `document.fonts.ready` and its own comment records this exact 14 % failure. Measured again: a warm cache AND a reload both still lay out on the fallback while `document.fonts.check()` returns **true**. Under `optional` the decision is made once, at load; the Font Loading API cannot revisit it. A guard that waits is a guard that hopes.
- **THE WIDENED GATE FOUND TWO MORE, both previously invisible** — exactly what the doctrine inside `sweepC5` predicts about every boundary this sweep has ever had: (1) « Nous envoyons votre demande de paiement de {montant} à l'opérateur. » at 0.34 under the real face; (2) « Rien n'est confirmé tant que l'opérateur n'a pas répondu. Nous ne dirons jamais le contraire. » at 0.22, on BOTH modes. Three defects, one race.
- **FIXED BY WELDING ONLY — not one word she reads was changed** (the « jamais\u00a0cachée » precedent). Escaped `\u00a0`, never raw bytes: the file still scans 0 raw U+00A0. Measured after: 0.553 (real) / 0.700 (fallback) at 360px, 0.639 / 0.808 at 320px.
- **THE GATE NOW DECIDES THE FACE INSTEAD OF RACING IT:** two deterministic regimes (same files re-declared `font-display: block`; or the woff2 aborted), each with a **guard on the guard** — `largeurDuTemoin` reads the ALREADY-LAID-OUT element, never a fresh probe, and fails loudly if the pin did not take. Without it a moved font URL would measure the fallback twice and pass by never looking, which is failure mode #1 in that same table.
- **MUTATION-PROVEN:** with the weld reverted the new gate goes red naming the sentence at « 14% of the block » — the CI failure, on demand. Restored, green.
- **EVIDENCE:** full board `scripts/run-gates.sh` **exit 0, zero `GATE FAILED`, 82 gates**; buyer-pwa 744/744 · storefront-service 448/448 · reseller-app 422/422 · attribution 43/43; Playwright **88 passed** (86 + the two new regimes).
- **DISCLOSED, NOT FIXED — owed a slice of its own:** at **320px under the fallback face**, « À payer maintenant : {X} FCFA » (`[data-role="payline-maintenant"]`) breaks before its amount and lands at **0.34** — a §6.1 money line dropping the figure onto a line of its own. The new gate is deliberately scoped to 360px (the width the existing sweep already covers) so that widening two axes in one slice cannot hide which one found what. This is recorded in the test itself, NOT carved out with an exemption.
- **NEXT:** founder to rule on the 320px payline; then this loop gains its second width.

'customised' : profilParam === 'vide' ? 'empty' : 'default'` — **a ternary chain with NO undefined branch**, so an absent `?demo-vitrine-profil` still yielded the truthy `'default'`. **`resolveStorefrontPort()` was therefore UNREACHABLE from the only route that carries real shared links**, and every real slug resolved against the demo adapter where only `aicha-4821` exists. Proven by **CONTENT-HASH IDENTIFICATION**, which is a fingerprint of the bytes:
  · deployed artifact (from the build job's own tar listing): **`assets/index-TazDux15.js`**

The artifact download URL was obtained and the fetch was attempted and DENIED. Content-hash identification is strong — arguably as strong as a byte-for-byte read — but it rests on vite's `[hash]` being a pure function of content, and it is an INFERENCE ABOUT the deployed bytes rather than a reading OF them.

## 2026-07-25 · OZ1 — BROWSE-SUPPLY-BINDING-1 (the supply hop becomes a SERVICE BINDING; SUPPLY_BASE stops existing) + DIAGNOSTIC-TARGET-1 + the no-store header · done — MERGED at `38c339a`, deployed, and **VERIFIED LIVE BY THE FOUNDER**: `status: ok` · `target.base: service-binding:OFFER` · `refusals: []` · both offers returned · Opportunités renders them on his device. *(Status corrected here on 2026-07-25: this heading still read « in-review — DO NOT MERGE » after the merge landed. - **THE FAULT THAT FORCED IT:** the supply read failed `unreachable · 404 · refusals []` **three times across three founder secret re-sets, including a typed one**. The diagnostic named the LAYER in one request — ruling out the app bundle, both app secrets, the gate, the wire password and the freshness bound — **then stopped helping**: it never said WHICH URL it had called, and a Worker secret is a value **nobody can read back** — not the founder, not me, not wrangler. Two wrong-value shapes reproduce the 404 exactly (a base carrying the singular path; the media host, whose fallthrough 404s anything it does not route). **And a third candidate is not a value at all: Cloudflare error 1042** — a Worker cannot `fetch` another Worker on the same workers.dev zone — with the critical fact that **this hop had NEVER succeeded**: every green probe came from a laptop.
- **THE FIX IS A SERVICE BINDING (founder order), right regardless of which hypothesis is true:** `[[services]] binding = "OFFER", service = "offer-service"` in `wrangler.toml`; `supply-source.ts` and `supply-collection.ts` take their fetcher from `env.OFFER.fetch`. Three properties make it the answer rather than a workaround: **(1)** it is the platform's own Worker-to-Worker mechanism — no network hop, no public URL, **no 1042 class at all**; **(2)** the configuration becomes **READABLE** — the binding name is versioned and reviewable in the repo, where the secret burned three founder round-trips because nobody could inspect it; **(3) `SUPPLY_BASE` stops existing as a failure point** — removed from the env shape entirely. **The exact failure mode we were stuck in stops being expressible.**
- **WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, deliberately:** boutik's Bearer gate stays load-bearing and **the `Authorization` header is still sent over the binding**, env-gated exactly as before (absent secret ⇒ no header, never a broken request). The seam philosophy survives intact: **resolve on the BINDING's presence** — `env.OFFER` present ⇒ `BoundSupplySource`, absent ⇒ `AbsentSupplySource` — the same honest-null discipline, with presence now visible in config rather than hidden in a secret. Tests stub the binding's fetch exactly as they stubbed `fetchImpl`.
- **THE E2E EXERCISES A REAL BINDING — no proof downgrade:** miniflare 4's `serviceBindings` runs a function-valued binding **through workerd**, so the e2e emulates boutik (fresh `asOf` computed at request time, one Bazin item, exact-path routing that 404s naming itself) and asserts the whole chain — binding fetch → canon envelope → freshness bound → identity sweep → `offers: [Bazin]`, `diagnostic.status: ok`, `diagnostic.target.base: service-binding:OFFER` — **inside the runtime production uses. The hop that never succeeded over a public URL is now exercised the way it will actually run.**
- **DIAGNOSTIC-TARGET-1 (built with it, per the standing order): A DIAGNOSTIC MUST NAME ITS TARGET, NOT ONLY ITS FAILURE.** The diagnostic now carries `target.base` — with a binding, the **binding name** — and, on any non-2xx, **`target.answeredBy`**: the upstream's self-reported `service` field when its body is service-shaped JSON, else the raw body **truncated to 120 chars** (an arbitrary upstream response never becomes an unbounded operator field). `answeredBy` **still matters with a binding**, because wrangler.toml can bind OFFER to the wrong service — and the responder naming itself is what exposes that in one read: « the OFFER binding reached MEDIA-SERVICE ». Both fields ride behind the same key; a service origin is a hostname, not a credential; the route is never included.

Asserted in the unit test AND through the real bundled Worker in the e2e. **The freshness instrument can no longer serve a cached answer.**
- **⚠ AUDIT (founder order — which fault paths can fail without naming their target):** `supply-source.describe()` **still collapses every failure to `undefined` with no target — DELIBERATE**: it is the buyer join's supply side, its caller omits products rather than diagnosing, and the operator diagnostic for the same wire is the collection route, which now names everything. ## 2026-07-25 · OZ1 — ⚠ THE FRESHNESS INSTRUMENT WAS THE LIAR: `/health` CAN BE SERVED FROM CACHE
- **Found by the founder while verifying the BROWSE-SUPPLY-1 deploy, and it lands on the instrument THIS LANE built (SERVICE-PROVENANCE-1).** He fetched `/health` and got **`release: a12b9a0`** — the OLD build — which looked exactly like a failed deploy. **It was not.** He read the DEPLOYED BUNDLE through the Cloudflare API instead: `supply-projections` is present, `SUPPLY_COLLECTION` appears **four times**, and the `diagnostic` field is there — **strings that exist only in `d143941` and later.** The route is live and the gate is in front of it.
- **THE DEFECT IN THE INSTRUMENT, stated as the founder stated it:** *"a check that cannot distinguish between the two states it is meant to separate is not a check."* A **CACHED 200 carrying an old `release` is indistinguishable from a STALE DEPLOY.** So `/health` is reliable for confirming **that a service answers**, and **NOT reliable for confirming a FRESH deploy** — which is the one job the stamp was built for.
- **THE MECHANISM, grounded rather than guessed:** `makeHealthFetch` (`packages/observability/src/health.ts:18-21`) returns `Response.json(...)` with **only the correlation header — NO `Cache-Control` at all** — and `withReadCors` (`services/storefront-service/src/index.ts:195`) adds CORS headers but no cache directive. A 200 GET with no cache directive is exactly what an edge may cache by default. **The journaled note that "Cloudflare bypasses cache for requests carrying an `Authorization` header" is the same fact from the other side: the key-gated routes were never cacheable, and `/health` — deliberately unauthenticated — always was.**

## 2026-07-24 · OZ1 — RESELLER-IDENTITY-1 (the identity survives a restart; the mint leaves Math.random) · MERGED (founder-approved) — `2b9ef8d` into main at `b3b7c10`, merge commit `7e02ad1`, ancestry read back from `origin/main`
- **The defect, found by the founder on a real preview walk:** `App.tsx:238` minted `digits` with `Math.random` inside a `useMemo` — stable per SESSION, fresh on every restart and every preview republish. His first shop was `aichomod-8291`; the next walk produced `chezaichamod-4911`. **The second consequence is the one that mattered:** `resellerId` (`rs-{digits}`) regenerated too, so **he was a DIFFERENT RESELLER every session** — storefronts unlinked from one person, no way back to yesterday's shop, and no browse-or-list flow can be honest on top of that.
- **Founder ruling — DEVICE-STORED identity, minted once, real identity deliberately deferred.** **HARD GATE, in plain words:** a device-stored id is **lost on reinstall**, **does not travel to a second phone**, and **CANNOT support a second reseller**. Before anyone but the founder onboards, real per-reseller identity is required — **the same gate already standing on the shared write key.**
- **THE MECHANISM DETAIL THAT MAKES PERSISTING ONE VALUE SUFFICIENT — journal it so nobody "tidies" it away:** `commandId` is **DERIVED** from the id (`create-${id}`), not independently random. `decideCreate` (`storefront-core.ts:122-126`) returns `idempotent` only on a **matching** commandId and **`collision`** otherwise. So persisting the digits makes the id AND the command id deterministic and a re-tap resolves to `idempotent`. **The obvious hygiene refactor — making `commandId` independently random — would break re-tap on every restart, turning every second launch into a collision.** Asserted in `identity.test.ts` so that refactor fails there first.
- **Built:** `src/identity/mint.ts` (pure — `digitsFromBytes` with **rejection sampling**, because 10 000 does not divide 2^16 and a naive `% 10000` would favour low values; `identityFromDigits`), `src/identity/store.ts` (the port + `loadOrMintIdentity` + an in-memory store for tests), `src/identity/expoStore.ts` (native, app-only). `App.tsx` now loads asynchronously: **`undefined` = still loading, `null` = mint or persist FAILED** — never a fabricated id.
- **THE HONESTY CONTRACT, which is the whole point:** **if the write fails, the identity is NOT returned.** A minted-but-unpersisted id works for exactly one session and then silently becomes a different reseller — the defect reappearing one layer down, and the same shape as the seam that answered « En ligne » having written nothing. A **read** failure is NOT fatal (indistinguishable from "nothing stored yet" → mint); a **write** failure is.
- **Storage choice, confirmed against the installed SDK rather than assumed:** `expo/bundledNativeModules.json` (SDK 54) pins **`expo-file-system ~19.0.23`** and **`expo-crypto ~15.0.9`**. Both are **first-party Expo SDK** modules, so **Expo Go ships their native halves by definition and this reaches the founder over the air with no rebuild** — the founder confirmed he runs Expo Go. A community module (AsyncStorage is bundled but community) would not carry that guarantee. **`expo-secure-store` was rejected on reasoning the founder accepted:** an id is **not a secret** (it appears in slugs and event payloads), the requirement is **durability**, and Keychain/Keystore adds real failure modes on low-end Android for protection nothing needs. `Paths.document` survives app-kill, reboot **and an EAS republish** — the same choice boutik made for its offline queue.
- **The slug promise becomes TRUE rather than merely intended:** with stored digits, `deriveShortCode` is stable and **her link stops moving**. That is a feature, not a side effect.
- **COPY — PROPOSED, NOT YET RULED (two new user-facing strings, lint-verified BEFORE proposing):** `k.publier.identite_attente` « Un instant — votre boutique se prépare. » (loading) and `k.publier.identite_absente` « Votre téléphone n'a pas pu enregistrer votre boutique. Rien n'a été envoyé. » (mint/persist failed). Both `neutral`/`status`; `copy-lint OK: 4 entries, 0 violations` on the candidate set, 6 and 8+4 words against a budget of 18. **Neither reads as a failure she caused; the second names the phone, not her, and states plainly that nothing was sent.** **AWAITING RULING BEFORE MERGE.**
- **ENTROPY, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN:** `digits` is FOUR digits because the canon shortCode shape is `[A-Z]{2,12}-[0-9]{4}` — **9 000 values**, thin as a global uniqueness key. Adequate ONLY because the founder is the sole reseller; it is subsumed by the real-identity hard gate above.
- **ORPHANS STAY ORPHANS (founder ruling):** at least two storefronts exist with different `resellerId`s, no products. **No adoption path, no migration, no reconciliation** — they are test data and inventing a migration would cost more than they are worth. **NAMED GAP: the service has NO storefront delete route** (`worker/index.ts:56-87` — no DELETE anywhere).
- **NAMED GAP, bigger than the orphans:** there is **NO UPDATE ROUTE**. `name`, `zone`, `category` and theme are **write-once at create**, so **anything she customises after create never reaches the service**. Named, not fixed.

## 2026-07-24 · OZ1 — MINT-PATH-ENTROPY-1 (inherited from canon, adapted — and a bundle scan PROVEN impossible for this property) · in-review — DO NOT MERGE
- **Founder ruling: shop-plus should carry boutik's mint-path gate, with the bundle scan load-bearing if it can be made clean.** It cannot, for this property — measured, not assumed.
- **WHY A BYTE-FOR-BYTE PORT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT NOTHING:** boutik's `check-mint-path-entropy.mjs:33` collects files matching `(command-id|commandId)*.{ts,mjs,js}` and **exits 0** with *"no mint path present in this repo"* when nothing matches (`:38-41`). Shop's mint lived in a **1 500-line `App.tsx`**, which matches no such pattern — **the ported gate would have printed OK and missed the very defect that shipped. A VACUOUS PASS IS WORSE THAN NO GATE, because it reads as coverage.**
- **THE BUNDLE SCAN IS NOT NOISY — IT IS BLIND. MEASURED ON THE REAL ARTIFACT.** `Math.random()` was deliberately planted in `App.tsx` and the bundle re-exported; the artifact was **byte-indistinguishable** from the clean one:

  | needle | clean bundle | WITH the defect planted |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Math.random` | 0 | **0** |
  | `random` | 1 | **1** |
  | `Math` | 1 | **1** |

  Hermes compiles `Math.random()` into a global lookup plus a property access, so **the literal `Math.random` never exists as a contiguous string**, and `Math` / `random` each appear **once** in the string table regardless of call-site count. **Presence AND count are both uninformative** — a bundle scan here would be always-green and assert nothing.
- **THE DIVISION OF LABOUR THAT FOLLOWS, and it is the durable lesson:** the **artifact scan** is load-bearing for **module ABSENCE** (a module's string literals ride into the bundle); the **source scan** is load-bearing for **CALL-SITE DISCIPLINE** (a compiled property access leaves no trace). Neither shape subsumes the other, and choosing by instinct rather than by measurement would have got this backwards.
- **Built `scripts/gates/mint-path-entropy.mjs`:** an **EXPLICIT NAMED FILE LIST** (not a glob that can silently match nothing) that **fails loudly if a named file is missing**, bans `Math.random` in stripped CODE (not prose — these files legitimately name the forbidden thing), and requires **at least one real CSPRNG draw** across the set so it cannot pass over an empty scan.
- **A repo-wide sweep was REJECTED as the noisy gate the founder ruled against:** it would flag `apps/buyer-pwa/src/cliente/flow.ts:161` (`Date.now() + Math.random()` for a **toast id** — a UI list key, not an idempotency key). *"A gate people learn to ignore is worse than none."*
- **PROVEN RED ON THE DEFECT:** the original `Math.random` mint planted back into `App.tsx` → `✘ App.tsx — Math.random in a MINT PATH`, **exit 1**. Restored → **exit 0**.

## 2026-07-24 · OZ1 — BUNDLE-GATE-VISION-1 (the positive control + the Hermes encoding constraint) · in-review — DO NOT MERGE
- **Why (cross-lane relay from APPS, then VERIFIED HERE rather than taken on faith):** APPS built the bundle-absence gate on this lane's finding and hit what this lane did not — **Hermes stores accented strings as UTF-16**, so a French fingerprint is invisible to a byte grep and the gate would pass vacuously forever. Our fingerprints (`demo://cover/`, `demo://avatar/`) are ASCII, **so the gate worked by luck rather than by reasoning.**
- **MEASURED ON THIS REPO'S OWN BUNDLE (`index-db85076a…hbc`), and the result is SHARPER than the relay:**
  - `'Mettre ma boutique en ligne'` → utf-8 **HIT**, utf-16le miss (pure ASCII)
  - `'Pas encore relié au service'` → utf-8 miss, utf-16le **HIT** (« é »)
  - `'Envoi en cours…'` → utf-8 miss, utf-16le **HIT** — **NO ACCENT AT ALL, only « … »**
  - **The rule is therefore NOT "accents are UTF-16".** Hermes stores a string in the narrow 8-bit encoding only when **EVERY** character fits; **a single non-ASCII character anywhere — an accent, a « guillemet », an ellipsis — flips the WHOLE string to UTF-16.** French copy here routinely carries all three, so **almost every user-facing French string is invisible to a byte scan.**
- **Why that is dangerous rather than merely interesting:** a French UI string is the INSTINCTIVE fingerprint choice, because that is what identifies a module in this codebase. Choosing one would make the gate **green, silent, and asserting nothing** — the same failure shape as a provenance stamp reading `dev` while looking healthy.
- **Built: the POSITIVE CONTROL.** The gate now proves it can **SEE** before it reports that it cannot **FIND**. Control = `X-Write-Key`, the write-gate header — **ASCII by protocol** (HTTP header names cannot be otherwise) and present in any bundle containing the real HTTP adapter, so it cannot be removed without removing the write path itself. **Exit 2 — a THIRD status, neither pass (0) nor violation (1)** — because "the scan is blind" is a different fact from "the adapter is present" and must never be reported as either.
- **PROVEN BLIND, not just proven green:** the control was temporarily pointed at `'Pas encore relié au service'` — a string that **IS** in the app but is UTF-16 — and the gate exited **2** with the blindness message. Restored: exit **0**, control found. **The demonstration is the vacuous-pass scenario itself, caught.**
- **Founder's standing rule, recorded:** *"A gate that cannot demonstrate its own vision is not evidence."*

## 2026-07-24 · OZ1 — ⚠ THE PATTERN, NAMED TWICE: A POPULATED FALLBACK IS DANGEROUS NOT BECAUSE IT CAN BE SELECTED BUT BECAUSE IT CAN BE PRESENT
- **Founder ruling: journal both instances as ONE pattern.** Twice this session a FABRICATION PATH nearly re-entered through a door nobody was watching:
  1. **The supply fallback itself (a1).** Every other env-gated fallback here degrades to something EMPTY (`resolveMediaStore`/`resolveStorefrontStore` → in-memory) — safe. A supply mock is **POPULATED**: it emits invented `productName`/`assetRefs`. A Worker that quietly fell back to it would serve fabricated products to a real buyer. Fixed by `AbsentSupplySource` + a two-branch resolver.
  2. **THE IMPORT (SUPPLY-WIRE-1) — the better catch, and it was nearly invisible.** `packages/supply-consumer/src/index.ts:8` is `export * from './mock.js'`, so importing the package **at its root** would have pulled the certified mock **into the deployed bundle** — silently undoing the unreachable-by-construction property built in (a1) and verified by the founder. **It would have passed every test**, because a mock merely *present* in a bundle is invisible to a test that never asks for it. Fixed with **subpath exports** (`/consumer`, `/read-model`) + a test asserting the package root is NEVER imported.
- **THE LESSON, in the founder's words:** *a populated fallback is dangerous not because it can be SELECTED but because it can be PRESENT.* Selection is testable; presence is not, unless something asserts the absence. **So the guard must be on the IMPORT GRAPH, not on the branch logic.**

## 2026-07-24 · OZ1 — SUPPLY-WIRE-AUTH-1 (shop's half: the service-to-service credential) · in-review — DO NOT MERGE
- **FOUNDER RULING, adopted in full:** per-caller bearer secret. Boutik holds `SUPPLY_READ_SECRET`; shop's Worker sends `Authorization: Bearer`; constant-time compare, fail-closed, ONE non-oracle 401 on the producer side; `wrangler secret put` on both sides — **never in `[vars]`, never in a repo, never in a report**.
- **⚖ THE DISTINCTION THAT IS LOAD-BEARING (founder asked it be kept in these words):** the **app write key SHIPS INSIDE A BUNDLE**, readable by anyone who downloads it — it stops **scanners**, not attackers, and **is not a real credential**. A **service-to-service secret NEVER LEAVES TWO WORKERS** — so it **is** one. **Do not reuse the app key here, and do not let anyone later decide one secret is simpler.** Asserted in a test: `supply-source.ts` may not name `STOREFRONT_WRITE_SECRET` or `X-Write-Key`.
- **PER-CALLER, not one platform secret:** rotating one caller cannot break the others, and a leak names its source. The eligibility wire instantiates the same shape with its own secret.
- **🎁 BONUS NEITHER OF US PLANNED (founder surfaced it — worth keeping):** **Cloudflare's cache automatically BYPASSES any request carrying an `Authorization` header.** We had already agreed the supply projection must never be cached — a cached copy hands back stale-but-honest truth while fresh truth exists, and the consumer would correctly refuse to act on it. **Choosing Bearer makes no-cache a PLATFORM PROPERTY rather than a discipline anyone has to remember.**
- **SEQUENCING — LOOSER THAN I PROPOSED, and the founder is right (nothing flows yet): SHOP SENDS FIRST, BOUTIK GATES SECOND.** I had proposed both sides in one cycle; that is correct once the wire carries traffic, but **it never has** — no real offer exists. Shop sending a header at an ungated producer is **harmless**; boutik gating before shop sends opens a **401 window**. So the header is **ENV-GATED: an absent secret means NO HEADER, never a broken request.** Neither lane blocks the other and there is no gap. APPS adds the gate after its current slice.
- **Evidence:** storefront-service **93/93** (89 → 93, +4: configured ⇒ `Bearer` sent · absent ⇒ no header AND the request still works · the resolver threads it from env, and a secret with NO base is still ABSENT because a credential is not a source · the credential is never the app write key) · typecheck 17 tasks · full test 21/21 · `run-gates.sh` **ALL GREEN** · frozen vault / money / sandbox ribbon / `VITE_STOREFRONT_BASE` untouched.
- **⚠ THE STANDING LIMIT, unchanged:** proven against **stubs of the producer's real shapes, not against boutik**. It becomes end-to-end **the day a real offer exists**, and not before.
- **Pending / next:** CI green on-branch → propose guarded merge. Then the deploy-freshness stamp. **NO merge without approval.**

## 2026-07-24 · OZ1 — REAL-PRODUCT-RENDER-1 piece (a2): membership + the server-side join · in-review — DO NOT MERGE
- **FOUNDER RULING BUILT: PUBLISH AUTO-APPENDS TO `curatedItems`.** Curation is about ARRANGEMENT (the « à la une et ordre » screen manages featuring and order over articles already present), not membership. A seller who publishes a product, opens her shop and sees nothing — needing a second screen to make it appear — is a design failure. `decideAddItem` appends **if absent**; a pid already present **keeps its position** and reports `already_present`, because reordering on republish would silently rearrange a shop she arranged.
- **THE TWO SOURCES CANNOT CONTRADICT (founder's reading, accepted and implemented):** `curatedItems` is the **membership statement, authoritative for the buyer**; the pid pointer is an **operational lookup** asked only *"which listing sells this pid, in this shop"* — a question with exactly one answer. It is never asked what is in her shop, so it is not a second answer to that question.
- **Cross-aggregate coordination lives at the COMPOSITION ROOT.** My first cut put the membership write inside the listing router, which made it depend on the `STOREFRONT` binding and **broke `listing-do.e2e` (5 failures)** — the standalone listing worker bundles `ListingDO` alone, so that binding cannot exist there. Corrected: the listing router writes only its own pid pointer; `worker/index.ts` (which holds both namespaces) makes the membership append after a successful publish. Neither aggregate depends on the other's namespace.
- **The read path joins server-side:** `GET /s/{slug}` walks `curatedItems` → pid pointer → the listing's **signed price** → supply description → `joinVitrineProduct`. **Every failure OMITS:** no resolvable listing (an inconsistency), a hidden listing, or an undescribable product. With no supply source configured — **the default, and the truth today** — every product is undescribable, so the payload carries **none**, and the e2e asserts exactly that rather than fabricated names.

## 2026-07-23 · OZ1 — STOREFRONT-DEPLOY-1 FIX (the deploy workflow was missing `pnpm build`) · done — MERGED at 568f33a (guarded: on-branch CI 30049442315 GREEN at the exact head 776c9c2 · frozen trees byte-identical 521449…/09a649… · frozen-path diff empty · founder approval on record, verified line-for-line)
- **What happened:** the first-ever deploy was attempted twice on `11ec2ad` — once by the founder (run 30048921907) and once by me at his instruction (run 30049163344). **Both failed at the same place, and NOT on Cloudflare:** the `bundle:worker:combined` step died with `✘ [ERROR] Could not resolve "@shop-plus/observability"` / `The module "./dist/index.js" was not found on the file system`. The deploy never reached `wrangler`, never touched the account token, never touched R2. So the R2-write-permission unknown is still untested — this was upstream of it.
- **Root cause (read-before-write; both workflows read in full):** `ci.yml:30` runs `pnpm build` before its gates, so by the time storefront-service's tests bundle the combined Worker (`pretest` hook), `@shop-plus/observability` has been compiled and its `exports → dist/index.js` exists. `storefront-deploy.yml` went straight from `pnpm install` to the bundle with **no build step** — so esbuild, inlining observability, could not resolve its `dist/index.js`. On-branch CI was green because CI never exercises the deploy workflow's bundle-without-build path — exactly the "green CI proves less than usual here" risk the founder flagged for this slice. His call was right.
- **Fix:** one line added to `storefront-deploy.yml` — `- run: pnpm build` between `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and the bundle, mirroring `ci.yml`. Nothing else changed (diff = the one step + its comment).
- **Proven, not asserted (local reproduction of the clean-runner condition):** stripped all 8 workspace `dist/` build outputs → `bundle:worker:combined` **failed, exit 1**, with the identical esbuild error; ran `pnpm build` (turbo, 10/10 tasks, exit 0) → same bundle **succeeded, exit 0**, producing `dist/worker/worker.mjs` (606 567 bytes) — the exact artifact `wrangler deploy` uploads.
- **Scope guard:** only `.github/workflows/storefront-deploy.yml` is a tracked change; frozen-vault diff (commerce-core, attribution-service) = 0 lines; rebuilt `dist/` is gitignored, not committed; wrangler.toml still correctly marked UNPROVEN (the deploy still has not succeeded).
- **FOUNDER CORRECTION (verify next iteration, then use):** a `workflow_dispatch` deploy does NOT always run the workflow file from `main`. Once the workflow exists on the default branch — which it now does — you can dispatch it against ANY branch and GitHub runs *that branch's* copy. So the NEXT deploy fix can be proven on-branch before merging, instead of merging each attempt to main. To be confirmed empirically on the next round; if it holds, use it — deploy debugging usually takes several rounds and this keeps main clean. (This first re-run still goes from `main`, since the fix is now there.)
- **DURABLE FIX — RECORD, DO NOT SLICE NOW (founder, while the deploy is mid-flight):** the missing `pnpm build` line was the symptom, not the disease. The real fragility: `bundle:worker:combined` depends on the workspace being built and *nothing declares that dependency* — it works locally only because a dev tree always has `dist/`. Any future workflow that bundles without building fails identically. The durable fix is to make the bundle script itself depend on the build (e.g. a `prebundle`/`prebundle:worker:combined` build hook, or the bundle depending on `pnpm build`), so the dependency is expressed once in the script, not re-remembered in every workflow. Deferred by founder ruling until the deploy is proven out — do not spend on it now.
- **Pending / next:** re-run storefront-deploy from `main`; report whether the DO migration applied + both classes (StorefrontDO, ListingDO) were created, whether R2 accepted a write, and the Worker URL if one exists. Then HOLD — do NOT wire VITE_STOREFRONT_BASE or MEDIA_PUBLIC_BASE without approval (founder must see the deploy prove out first). A first-deploy R2 permission failure is EXPECTED (token has only ever created the bucket) and is a dashboard token fix, not a code change.

But the 404.html sends every deep link to `/shop-plus/?/…` → `index.html` = **that wrapper**, which discarded the `?/v/…` restore query and forced its own landing — so **no deep link ever restored**, independent of defect 1. (And the target `?demo-journey` was the route I just retired.)
  3. **manifest at absolute-root `/manifest.webmanifest`** (404.html link) — wrong host path on the sub-path deploy.
- **FIX (built):**
  1. `index.html` restore script **pins a `<base href="{app-root}">`** (`location.pathname`, e.g. `/shop-plus/`) BEFORE the `replaceState`, so `./assets/*` always resolve to the app root regardless of the restored deep path. Keeps vite base `'./'` — no preview/e2e churn, portable to any deploy path. No-op on normal loads (no `?/`).
  2. pwa-preview **ships `dist` AS-IS** (removed the redirect-wrapper step) — the deployed `index.html` is the real app (with the restore script), so `/shop-plus/?/…` restores correctly. The deployed root is the app's real root (S3 DÉCOUVERTE).
  3. manifest consistency: `public/404.html` link → `/shop-plus/manifest.webmanifest`; `public/manifest.webmanifest` gains `id`+`start_url`+`scope` = `/shop-plus/`. `deployBaseFromPath`/`vitrineHref` were already correct (dynamic base from pathname → `/shop-plus`) and now AGREE.
- **REPRODUCED + PROVEN (the founder's ask — a real Pages e2e):** NEW `scripts/pages-emulator.mjs` (project sub-path + serve-file-else-404.html, the behaviour vite preview cannot reproduce) wired as a second Playwright webServer (:4174). NEW `e2e/deploy-base.spec.ts` (3 tests, GREEN): bare origin → `/shop-plus/` redirect; **`/shop-plus/v/aicha-4821` deep link BOOTS the vitrine** (404 → restore → `<base>`-pin → assets load, asserting **zero `.js/.css/.woff2` 404s during boot** — non-vacuous: the old code 404s the module script here); `/shop-plus/s/aicha-4821?pid=p2` boots the achat S1 for the real product (Pagne wax). URL restored to the canon `/v/…` / `/s/…`.

## 2026-07-11 · CI INCIDENT #3 (expo-preview red on its first armed runs) · fixed on main `21400d0`
- **Both armed `expo-preview` runs were red** (this repo ×2; boutik ×4, sera ×2 — one shared defect). Diagnosis from the complete Actions logs (pulled via API, log-copied): token check, checkout, install, `eas init --non-interactive --force` (`✔ Project successfully linked (ID: 3436dab2-922f-4f80-beeb-e17e85f1f099)`) and `update:configure` (`✔ Configured updates.url`) all PASSED — the failure is the third command's bundling: `SyntaxError: index.ts: Cannot find module 'babel-preset-expo'`, identical across the three repos. The token and the founder's account are NOT the cause.
- **Root cause (config-class, reproduced in boutik's cold clone, byte-identical error):** `babel.config.js` names `babel-preset-expo`; the app manifest never declared it; pnpm strict isolation leaves it unresolvable from the app directory on a fresh install; babel has no fallback (direct `@babel/core` transform emulation).
- **Why WO-4.0's evidence missed it (failure-mode #8, named):** the `expo start --offline` boot probe transforms nothing until a client connects, and local exports silently reused Metro's cross-directory content-hash cache (`$TMPDIR/metro-cache`), bypassing babel. Standing lesson: bundling evidence = a cache-isolated `expo export`, never a dev-server boot line.
- **Fix `21400d0`:** `babel-preset-expo ~13.2.5` (expo 53.0.27's own declared range) added to `apps/reseller-app` devDependencies; lockfile by regeneration (+3 lines, zero new packages, dup-key assert 0). Evidence: resolve-from-app-dir OK · gates exit 0 (ALL GATES GREEN) · cache-isolated export exit 0 (579 modules bundled) · boutik cold-clone proof of the identical fix passed.
- **The founder's next expo-preview runs are the only closure** — this entry claims the local reproduction and fix, never the publish.

  5. **A 201 over a 404.** The pointer write was `.catch(() => undefined)` with the Response DISCARDED; `.catch` traps a rejection, not a 404 Response. Upload against a missing storefront answered `201 live` while the DO said absent → success toast over a slot spinning « ENVOI… » forever.
  6. **« Retirer la couverture » removed nothing** — local state only, no remove route; the cliente kept seeing the old cover and it returned on the next read.

### 2026-07-28 (later) · MEDIA-2 round 3 — a THIRD verifier, five blockers, and vacuous tests I wrote myself
- **The tests I added in round 2 were vacuous, and mutation proved it.** A verifier scrambled EVERY arm of the failure-reason map (offline → « trop lourde », too_large → « publiez votre boutique ») and all four of my new tests stayed green (34/34); gutting `coverTo` to `return sf` left customize.test.ts green (13/13); deleting the transition that puts the cover into the error state left it green too. They were `readFileSync` + `toContain` assertions: they proved two substrings existed SOMEWHERE in a file, never that they belonged to each other. **Failure mode #7, written by my own hand, inside the commit whose message claimed to have fixed these very messages.** The lesson is not « add more tests » — it is that a test which cannot execute the thing it names is not evidence.
- **FIX:** the mapping is now a pure module (`upload-outcome.ts`) tested by CALLING it (`test/upload-outcome.test.ts`, 6 behavioural tests), and `coverTo` has real tests. Mutation-proven: the scramble now fails 2, the shipped weight-default bug fails 3, the title mutation fails 1, `coverTo → return sf` fails 1, dropping the url again fails 1.
- **BLOCKER 1 — every 502 still reached her as « Essayez une image plus légère ».** Round 2 made the service's named reason SURVIVE the HTTP boundary and then discarded it at the mapping. `storefront_absent`, `not_pointed`, `storefront_unreachable`, `unauthorized`, `empty`, `bad_request` and every 5xx fell through to the weight default — and `storefront_absent` is a state where NO photo of ANY weight can ever succeed. Now every service reason is mapped by name, service faults get a blameless sentence (« Ce n'est pas votre photo »), and the DEFAULT is cause-free: an unknown reason must not guess weight.
- **BLOCKER 2 — `coverTo` dropped `cover.url`.** MEDIA-1 added `url?` to the cover shape and never updated the constructor. A failed REPLACEMENT walked live → uploading → error → none and lost the address, so her app said « Ajouter une couverture » over a shop whose cliente was still seeing the photograph, with no in-screen recovery (the adoption effect is keyed on `updatedAt`, which never moved).
- **BLOCKER 3 — the error card contradicted itself.** Hard-coded title « Photo pas envoyée » sat above the body « Photo envoyée, pas encore visible » on the `not_confirmed` path — where the upload HAD succeeded and only the confirming read failed. The title follows the reason now.
- **BLOCKER 4 — the in-flight lock started after the slow half.** `setAvatarSending(true)` / `coverTo(…,'uploading')` ran AFTER `await pickPhoto()`, but the decode + resize + re-encode of a 12 MP photo is the slowest leg on a 1 GB phone and happens back on the screen. The guard covered only the network. Locked before the pick now — and a CANCELLED pick restores the cover she actually has rather than falling to `'none'`.
- **BLOCKER 5 — `uploadWired` was never false.** The App passes `onUploadCover`/`onUploadAvatar` unconditionally, so the documented « absent ⇒ the slot stays inert » guard did not exist. On an unconfigured build she could grant photo access, sit through a full decode, and then be told to « publier votre boutique » — which cannot fix a build with no service URL. The slot is now gated on `serviceUnconfigured !== true && shopIsLive`, and an inert slot SAYS why.
- **EVIDENCE:** workspace typecheck 19/19 · `TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm test` 23/23 tasks (reseller-app 319/319, buyer-pwa 214/214, storefront-service 201/201, commerce-core 86/86, attribution 43/43) · `run-gates.sh` ALL GATES GREEN · copy-lint 449/0 and 179/0 · frozen vault 0 lines.
- **STILL NOT BUILT, not pretended:** cover REMOVAL (no route); a moderation approve route; slice 3. **STILL UNVERIFIED:** `MEDIA_PUBLIC_BASE` matches the deployed origin (sandbox proxy refuses workers.dev) — first thing to check after deploy; and everything device-side.
- **STATE: BUILT · local green · DO NOT MERGE until the founder approves.**

### 2026-07-29 · FIELD FIX MERGED `9359847` — the loading state stopped lying
- **Founder field report:** « voir ma boutique en ligne » showed « Ce lien ne mène à aucune boutique » and only THEN the boutique. **Cause, ours:** `mountVitrine`'s render opened with `if (etat !== 'invalid' && !resolved) etat = 'invalid'` — and `load()` calls `render('loading', undefined)`. So the guard rewrote the LOADING state to the terminal not-found: the designed skeleton NEVER rendered on a real visit, and every load painted a dead-link card for the whole network round-trip. A terminal error standing in for a network wait is exactly what the honest-states law forbids.
- **Fix:** the buried rule is now the pure `etatForRender(etat, hasResolved)` — only `ready`/`empty` (the states that dereference the storefront) fall back to `invalid`; `loading`/`offline`/`invalid` pass through. Same treatment the ENTETES-B verifier demanded for the `?entete=` wiring: a rule nobody could test became a named function with executed pins.
- **Mutation-checked before shipping:** restoring the old logic fails 2 of the 3 new tests; the fix passes all 3. buyer-pwa 350/350 · tsc clean · run-gates ALL GREEN · vault 0 · CI green at `73da9a1`.
- **Merge `9359847`** (`--no-ff`): tree diff vs approved sha EMPTY · vault 0 · origin/main re-read, ancestry asserted.
- **Lesson for the books:** this shipped because no test ever executed the mount's state sequence (node env, no DOM). The house answer is the one applied here — extract the decision, pin it pure. Any future state rule buried inline in `mountVitrine` is a repeat waiting to happen.

### 2026-07-29 · SP3.2a round 3 — the SECOND verifier broke MY fix, on the money path
- **Founder instruction: « Do it with the fresh verifier. » It paid for itself immediately.** Round 2's request-key fingerprint was a **TOCTOU across two Durable Objects**: the router read the QUOTE object (« nothing issued ») and then wrote the KEY POINTER object, and two concurrent requests could interleave between those steps. The verifier reproduced, over raw sockets, a buyer being served **another shop's price** — HTTP 200, no error, **durable**, surviving a real restart, with the legitimate first intent locked out at 409. ~1/250 rounds in a harness that barely overlaps requests; wider on real workerd. My `/key/rebind` comment asserted the router's ordering as an invariant — it was an assumption, and the verifier falsified it.
- **THE FIX — one object owns the question and the answer:** the intent fingerprint now lives BESIDE THE QUOTE'S BYTES, written in the same act, inside the object that owns them. « Which intent does this quote answer » became a single-object read that cannot interleave. `/key/rebind` is DELETED (dead code on a money path is a trap); the key pointer's only job is « which id does this key name », minted once, constant forever, holding no opinion about intent. The race-LOSER branch (`quote_id_exists`) now compares intent too — that branch is exactly where the foreign total reached a buyer.
- **PROVEN AGAINST THE VERIFIER'S OWN REPRO:** its `p3e-repro.mjs` (250 rounds × 6 concurrent requests, two shops at 12 500 and 15 000) → **0 anomalous rounds out of 250**, against ~1/250 before. Two permanent regression pins added: the racing-intents test (nobody receives a foreign total; the loser stays refused sequentially AND across a restart) and a refusal-retry test (a key whose only attempt refused stays usable for delivery/attribution/listing refusals alike).
- **Verifier finding #2 also fixed:** `attributionResellerId: ""` returned a shape error while the code's own comment promised the named `attribution_missing`; an empty string now means « nobody is locked » and reaches that refusal, while a non-string stays a 400.

The harness/`?demo-cliente=` path keeps `composeQuote` so a preview with no service reachable still works.

Both sides now reduce to their **city component** for the lookup — no new rows, no second tariff, unserviceable still the default, and the quote still names the caller's own strings. **Consequence stated, not discovered: the quartier does not change the price until Séra prices for real.**

The builder then found the trigger neither of us named: the request key is stable, so a **RELOAD** lands on the same quote and one-per-fetch was still not enough. It is now persisted per QUOTE ID. Also: « Pas de connexion » was shown for four different failures including « the server answered something unreadable »; and the checked body was passed through raw under a type claiming eight fields.
- **FIRST FRESH VERIFIER PASS: FAIL — eight defects, six blockers.** In a real Chromium against a hostile service (24 attacks, 10 mutations, a 30-case zone matrix):

### 2026-07-30 · SP3.3a — the payment legs, server-side and durable. FOUR ROUNDS, three verifier passes (two FAIL), ten defects.
- **What shipped:** an order is created from a RESERVED quote, its legs derived from the mode and the frozen quote bytes (§5.5 — FULL_PREPAY: one `checkout` leg of `buyerTotal`; door mode: `checkout` of D + `door` DUE of `productSubtotal`), a charge goes out through a provider port, and the order confirms ONLY on a signed webhook the frozen vault validates to the franc against the immutable Quote. One DO per order id, derived from the quote id, so one quote cannot grow two orders. **Not one payment decision is re-implemented** — `order-spine`/`order-machine`/`ledger`/the certified mock are the vault's, and the DO stores the inputs the vault accepted and replays them.
- **The webhook is the only route that can declare money received**, and is treated that way: its OWN secret (a `wrangler secret`, never `[vars]`), its own header, FAIL CLOSED when unset, authenticated at the composition root BEFORE any dispatch so a rejection never reaches a DO and the 401 is never an existence oracle.
- **The reservation is PROVEN, not assumed** — the fix for the hijack flag journalled at SP3.2a. `CheckoutDO` exposes no way to ASK who holds a quote without TAKING the hold, so the decided hold is copied into the order's own object at the moment the vault grants it (four strings, no money, single-object read, fails CLOSED when lost).
- **VERIFIER PASS 1 — FAIL. Two money/ownership defects and an undefended fail-closed guard:**
  1. **A RETRY MINTED A NEW PROVIDER IDEMPOTENCY KEY — a duplicate charge, which SP-I13 forbids in those words.** One identifier did two jobs: the state machine REQUIRES a new audit attempt id on the retry edge, the provider requires a STABLE key (the certified mock says so in its own header). Reproduced from an `initiateCharge` TIMEOUT — the canonically ambiguous case — then a retry: two keys for one 12 500 F leg, one recorded leg, the second webhook refused `out_of_order` and lost. **Buyer debited twice, no alert, no reconciliation case, no refund path.** FIXED: `att-` is the audit id and never reaches the provider; `pk-` belongs to the `(order, legType)` pair, minted once, persisted before the charge, reused by every retry.
  2. **THE RESERVATION RECEIPT COULD BE FLIPPED.** It took `holderRef` from the REQUEST and the ids from the RESPONSE, and the vault replays a hold idempotently — so replaying a victim's reserve `commandId` under your own holder renamed the holder, refused HER order and created YOURS while CheckoutDO still held her reservation. FIXED: a receipt for a given `reservationId` is IMMUTABLE (an idempotent replay is by definition not a new decision); a different id needs a STRICTLY LATER expiry.
  3. **`auth.ts`'s fail-closed guard was defended by nothing** — `secret.length > 0 && match` → `match` passed 342/342, and `timingSafeEqual('','')` is true, so an unset webhook secret plus no header would have authenticated EVERY webhook. Anyone could declare any order paid, into real custody and real settlement. Plus: the charged amount could drift from the recorded amount; the receipt monotonicity guard and the webhook `order_id` alphabet were undefended; authorization ran AFTER the idempotency cache; the results lookup walked the prototype chain; and the mock guard scanned import SPECIFIERS only — so `payment-port.ts`'s barrel import was ALREADY inside the hole it claimed to close (both mocks smuggled in, 30/30 green).
- **VERIFIER PASS 2 — FAIL, and the right kind.** Every round-1 finding was closed AT RUNTIME (each attack re-run, none reproduced), but four mutations survived — one re-opening the duplicate charge **with a single line while 350/350 stayed green**. Root cause: **the test manufactured the evidence it audited** — it asserted the key the object WROTE and fabricated the confirming webhook from that same value. Failure mode #7 on the highest-stakes line in the repo. FIXED by reading the PORT'S OWN ANSWER (`collectRef`, built by the provider from the key it actually saw) and deriving every fabricated event from the OBSERVED value.
  · The durability claim was a COMMENT (moving the put after the charge survived). Made **unwriteable-wrong**: the key handed to the provider is the one STORAGE ANSWERS WITH — put, read back, refuse `leg_key_not_durable`, then charge. **The verifier's own judgement, recorded: this buys ORDERING, not crash safety** (DO storage serves reads from the write buffer; the crash window is closed by workerd's output gate, which was already true). Kept for the ordering guarantee, not credited with durability.
  · The amount fix was two-edit reversible ⇒ trust moved out of the test and into the code: a divergence between the port's echo and the leg is now a REFUSAL that records nothing. Neither number is trusted.
  · The mock guard's namespace and **dynamic** import holes — the second would have admitted a SUPPLY mock, the exact thing that test exists to stop. All three unreadable forms now banned outright.
- **VERIFIER PASS 3 — PASS WITH NOTES, one note:** both new refusals **stranded the order at `payment_pending` with no exit** — persisted before the guard, no `failPayment`, and the retry branch needs `payment_failed`. Every buyer escape returned `payment_pending` forever; the reservation never released (the E2 rule fires on payment failure). Latent (neither fault can fire today) but it had to close before SP3.3b writes copy: **when the only honest sentence for a state is a promise the backend cannot keep, the state is wrong, not the copy.** FIXED: both end the attempt through the vault's `failPayment`, so the ordinary retry path applies — safe precisely because of round 2, since a retry reuses the leg key and cannot double-collect.
- **THE FIX HAD A DEFECT OF ITS OWN, found by running the verifier's probe against it:** the fault's `command_id` was keyed on `commandId`, which the spine dedupes on — so the retry's fault input was absorbed as a duplicate and the order stranded again through a different door. Now keyed on the ATTEMPT id, which is minted per attempt and cannot repeat. **Reasoning missed it; the probe caught it.**
- **⏳ OPEN DECISIONS, NOT CLOSED HERE (§7):**
  · **The aggregator, the BCEAO perimeter, two-leg/refund fees and auth-capture stay open (Real-Money Gate).** No aggregator is named in code, config or comment; the certified sandbox is the only implementation. Whether a DEFINITELY-REJECTED charge may be retried under a fresh key is aggregator semantics — not modelled; the documented safest default (one stable key per leg, every retry) is implemented and the open question is named at the mint site.
  · **`PaymentFailureReason` has no value that fits a self-refusal.** `charge_rejected | charge_timeout | webhook_never_arrived` — no provider rejected anything, nothing timed out, no webhook was expected. `charge_rejected` is used as the safest default; **a fourth value is a frozen-vault + `contracts/` change and therefore the founder's call.** **⚠ STANDING CONSTRAINT, verifier's recommendation, adopted: NO refund or reconciliation logic may key on this reason until that fourth value exists.** It is audit metadata only today — nothing in the repo reads `lastPaymentFailure` — and E3 refund routing that read `charge_rejected` as « definitely no money » would be WRONG for `provider_amount_divergence`, where a charge went out and its amount is in doubt. The fault IS named in the `command_id` (`ord-fault-{fault}-{attemptId}`) so the audit still says which defence ended the attempt.
- **RESIDUAL, ACCEPTED WITH REASONS:** reverting BOTH refusal call sites to the stranding return is not killed by any permanent test (358/358 green), because neither fault can be triggered at runtime. The **decision** half is fully defended (three named tests, all killed by mutation); the **call sites** are covered by a recorded probe. The two ways to close it — a production fault-injection seam on a money path, or a test that boots Miniflare on a deliberately faulty bundle inside `worker/` (which the mock-guard test walks) — both cost more than the gap. **Left open on purpose.**
- **⚠ CARRIED, NOT CLOSED:** a webhook arriving BEFORE create answers `404 unknown_order`; a provider that treats 404 as non-retryable would silently drop a valid confirmation. Belongs with the aggregator decision. · **Option B has never crossed workerd end to end** (`networkReliableZones` ships empty, so issuance refuses it) — covered by value and by the gate driver; no fake eligibility was wired to reach it. · `POST /storefronts` returns a bare **500** for a malformed short code (SP1-era, outside this slice) where a named 400 belongs.
- **EVIDENCE (verified by ME at this head, cache purged so nothing could be replayed):** storefront-service **358/358** (18 files) · repo-wide **35/35, 0 cached** · `run-gates.sh` **ALL GREEN, 0 GATE FAILED** including the funded-legs gate now exercising the NEW path in both modes and a negative fixture whose confirmed order is one franc short · frozen vault **0** · `checkout-core.ts` + `checkout-do.ts` **0** vs `origin/main`. Verifier mutation totals across passes: 23 run / 19 killed, then 15 run / 10 killed with the five survivors each individually justified (two provably equivalent mutants, three unreachable without fault injection).
- **NOT VERIFIED:** `wrangler deploy` of the `ORDER` binding and the `v3` migration; `PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` must be set out-of-band or every webhook is 401 by design (orders can be created and charged but never confirmed).

### 2026-07-30 · SP3.3b1 — the §6.1 two-option screen. FIVE ROUNDS, three verifier passes, and the same lesson four times.
- **What shipped:** C5 now meets §6.1 — both options with A labelled « recommandé », each body quoted verbatim from the spec, the non-refundable-delivery warning, the two bold lines per mode (« À payer maintenant : X » / « À payer à la livraison : Y »), the total once, and the one-line replay before payment. **Every franc on the screen is a server byte**: each mode's own `amountPaidAtCheckout`/`amountDueAtDelivery`, carried rather than re-derived. The spec's « total = X+Y » is a statement about what the server's numbers MEAN — the total rendered is `buyerTotal`, never a client sum.
- **The screen stopped applying the CLIENT'S rule about what a payment mode means** (total-for-A, fee-for-B). That rule now survives in exactly one place — `payezMaintenant`, used by C6 only — labelled as SP3.3b2's to remove.
- **FOUNDER RULING (2026-07-30):** the replay uses §6.1's normative sentence in BOTH modes, so « Tout payer maintenant » replays as « … et 0 FCFA à la livraison — d'accord ? ». The screen had been taking two positions at once (the card said `0 FCFA`, the replay said « rien ») with two tests locking the opposite conventions. §6.1 is normative and gives ONE sentence; writing a second is interpreting a money sentence, which is a §7 stop. Recorded at the site with the reasoning. One existing assertion changed under explicit authorisation; both remain exact-byte.
- **THE THREAD THAT RUNS THROUGH ALL FIVE ROUNDS — a guard was narrowed four times, and each narrowing hid a real defect:**
  1. **Scoped by SELECTOR.** « Livraison Séra — jamais cachée » truncated to « Livraison Séra — ja… », deleting the trust claim of the row that exists to make it. §5 names that test in terms. Fixed; a measured 360px gate added.
  2. **Scoped by ELEMENT.** The same orphan defect sat one element below, on the §6.1 replay: « d'accord ? » — the question she is asked to agree to — stranded alone at **0.286** of the block, below the 0.35 bar the project already enforced one element above. Nobody asked whether any OTHER sentence had it. The sweep now enumerates text blocks **structurally** — every block-level box whose element children are all inline, which excludes bills and option rows whose « lines » are layout, not sentences.
  3. **Scoped by STATE.** The builder's first widened sweep PASSED while the replay was still broken: C5 mounts with no mode chosen, so the replay did not exist yet. It now runs in all three states and **asserts the replay was in the swept set**.
  4. **Scoped by COMPUTED DISPLAY, then by FIXTURE AMOUNT.** The CTA — the screen's primary action, the one element carrying an amount — computed to `inline-block` and was rejected before a ratio was ever taken; and the sweep only ever ran against one 12 500 basket, where nothing else wraps. Both closed: `display: block` + a CTA-in-swept-set assertion, and a second sweep at a large basket, proven content-specific (the round-4 spec passes the mutation the round-5 spec catches).
- **A METRIC BUG THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE GATE A LIE:** the ratio denominator was `clientWidth` (unzoomed) while the line rects come back scaled by the flow's `zoom: 1.15` — **every ratio inflated 15%, lowering the bar to an effective 0.30.** Fixed and written into the test's comment. **⚠ The round-4 commit message `59fac94` quotes 0.836; the true figure is 0.727 (0.727 × 1.15 = 0.836) — the commit text carries the buggy number and history was not rewritten. The verifier proved the correction independently: reverting the fix prints 29%, matching the hand-measured 0.286.** I repeated 0.836 to the founder and corrected it in the next message.
- **Also closed:** the mode-A replay's Y leg was asserted by PREFIX only, so hardcoding it to zero passed all 525 tests · `rediteFin`/`titreBFin` are now pinned as substrings, so the `.replace` glue cannot silently become a no-op (the em-dash mutation passed 525 unit tests and only failed 40 s later in Playwright) · the placeholder allowlist is per-FIELD, not per-table (planting `{D}` in a field filled with `{X, Y}` used to pass and would have shipped the literal token).
- **THE LINT GATE'S REACH, twice corrected:** it read only its own tables while printing that the forbidden words appear nowhere — « séquestre » planted in `index.html` passed. The raw scan went 31 → **40 files** across `index.html`, `public/`, `i18n/` and CSS, and **the success message now names what is linted AND what is not**, so the remaining gap is visible instead of implied away. The extractor was deliberately NOT widened — that is its own slice.
- **THE `text-wrap: balance` INCIDENT, worth keeping:** the first wrap fix used it, and `no-wallet-no-funds` failed the build because that gate bans the word anywhere in source (Ten Laws #2). **No exception was carved.** The replacement is better: a no-wrap tail makes the break deterministic on every engine, including the 2018 WebView Ten Laws #7 puts first, which `text-wrap` would not support anyway.
- **⚠ ACCEPTED MARGIN, decided not discovered:** once the CTA wraps, its last line is always « maintenant » at **0.354** — 1.1% above the bar, fixed regardless of amount. NOT glued, on the stylesheet's own rule: a nowrap unit inside an amount-carrying label can force a horizontal scroll, and this case needs a delivery fee near a million francs, so it is unreachable on any real tariff. Revisit if the CTA copy changes.
- **⚠ §6.1 REQUIREMENT OUTSTANDING: the per-option audio note is NOT built.** There is no recorded French take for the two options, and a player wired to a generated tone would be a mock impersonating a voice on the money screen (Ten Laws #5, and Execution Contract §3 on certified mocks). Named in a comment beside the cards so the omission is visible in the code. **It needs two short recordings from the founder.**

### 2026-07-31 · ENTETES-H COMPLETE — the twenty-five new headers are built, and all 31 canon keys draw

Canon vocabulary reached 31 keys at v2.4.0 (`65f6c80`); the picker sat at eleven while each unit was built, and closed the gap with the last one.   - What actually happens: `commit.gpgsign=true` with `gpg.format=ssh` and `gpg.ssh.program=/tmp/code-sign` → `/opt/env-runner/environment-manager`, a REMOTE signing helper. It holds the private key; the empty local `.pub` is irrelevant to it. One stable ed25519 key across the whole run: `ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIKy87HxSEheG8vEPhSs9u2KZCtVErAQfpmprtUJCZ2w7`.
  - Proven, not assumed: 40/40 recent commits carry a `gpgsig` SSHSIG header, and five of them (spanning the run, `b3176f3` to `1f05f9a`) were verified from first principles — RFC 8032 ed25519 by hand, because this image has no `ssh-keygen` and its `cryptography` wheel is broken. All VALID, namespace `git`, sha512. The checker carries a negative control: one flipped byte of the commit message makes it report INVALID, so the PASS discriminates.
  - ~~The key is not registered on the GitHub account, so GitHub shows these commits unverified.~~ **WRONG AGAIN — and this time I measured instead of guessing.** GitHub's API reports `verified: true, reason: valid` for these commits (`b3176f3`, `27ede59`, `7358cf9`, spanning the run). They are attributed to the GitHub account **`claude`** — author and committer — because `noreply@anthropic.com` belongs to it and the signing key is registered there. **There is no founder-side action here, and registering that key on the founder's own account would be WRONG**: it would assert Anthropic's key is his.
  - Consequence for branch protection: a « Require signed commits » rule gates on exactly that `verified` flag, which is already true, so it would NOT block these commits. **NOT directly tested** — this session's token is read-only (`admin: false`) and the proxy refuses writes to both `/branches/*/protection/required_signatures` and `/rulesets` (403 each). Measured: the verification status. Inferred: the rule's decision from it. The line between those two is the point.
  - **Debt I created and cannot clean up:** the scratch branch `claude/scratch-signing-test` — an exact copy of `main` at `7358cf9`, no unique commits. The git proxy permits branch CREATION but refuses deletion (403 on `git push --delete` and on the API ref delete). The founder has to remove it. I should have checked whether I could delete a branch before creating one.
  - Local `git verify-commit` cannot work in this image at all (no `ssh-keygen`; git would route verification through the signing helper and report `B`, which reads as BAD). I set `gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile`, saw it produce that misleading `B`, and reverted it — an honest `N` beats a false alarm.
